subsystems.name: Propulsion
subsystems.role: generates thrust for liftoff, ascent and powered landing.

subsystems.name: Propellant tanks and primary structure
subsystems.role: holds cryogenic propellants and carries the vehicle's loads.
parts: stainless steel or aluminium-lithium tank barrels

subsystems.name: Avionics and flight control
subsystems.role: guides the vehicle through ascent, reentry and landing.

subsystems.name: Thermal protection system
subsystems.role: protects the booster and upper stage from reentry heating.

subsystems.name: Landing and recovery system
subsystems.role: enables the booster to return and be reused.

subsystems.name: Payload integration and separation
subsystems.role: carries and deploys payloads into orbit.

buildSteps.title: Design and simulate
buildSteps.detail: Computational fluid dynamics and finite element analysis shape tanks, engines and the reentry profile before any metal is cut.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate tanks
buildSteps.detail: Metal sheets (stainless steel or aluminium-lithium) are rolled into rings, welded into barrels and domes, and inspected for defects.

buildSteps.title: Build engines
buildSteps.detail: Turbopumps, injectors and nozzles are machined and assembled, then each engine is test-fired individually.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the stage
buildSteps.detail: Engines are integrated with the thrust structure, tanks are attached, and plumbing for propellant and pressurant lines is installed.

buildSteps.title: Install avionics and thermal protection
buildSteps.detail: Wiring and sensors are run, flight computers are mounted, and heat shield tiles and insulation are applied.

buildSteps.title: Integrate payload section
buildSteps.detail: The fairing or payload bay, separation systems and payload adapter are attached to the upper stage.

buildSteps.title: Test and launch
buildSteps.detail: An integrated static fire is performed at the pad; after launch the booster returns for landing or catch, is refurbished, and is reused.

prerequisites.why: engines must throttle deeply and survive multiple firings without full refurbishment.
tanks and frames must be light enough to leave payload capacity while withstanding launch and reentry loads.
the booster must hit a small landing zone or catch point after a hypersonic reentry.
large reusable stages face heating that ceramic tiles or metallic shields can handle only with careful inspection and repair.
reuse cadence, not payload capacity, limits how quickly orbital infrastructure can grow.

pathway.milestone: partially reusable heavy-lift vehicles (e.g. SpaceX Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy) and fully reusable super-heavy vehicles in flight test (e.g. SpaceX Starship).
pathway.unlocks: routine access to space for large payloads and satellite constellations.

pathway.milestone: fully reusable super-heavy vehicles enter commercial service with rapid reuse.
pathway.unlocks: hundred-tonne payloads at lower cost and orbital tanker flights.

pathway.milestone: orbital refueling and propellant depots become operational.
pathway.unlocks: crewed lunar and Mars missions, large space telescopes, and orbital construction.

pathway.milestone: high-cadence spaceports and point-to-point transport mature.
pathway.unlocks: space-based solar power, large-scale orbital manufacturing, and fast global transport.
